sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.used_for: §1 defines 'Special Links' as tagged links in the formats Amazon provides; §5 requires the statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.' on the Site; §5 also bars misrepresenting or embellishing the Amazon relationship.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Participation Requirements, Commission Income Statement, Products Statement, IP License, Trademark Guidelines)
sources.method: fetched (Commission Income Statement §1, Participation Requirements (g), (q), (s), (u), (v), (w), Trademark Guidelines 3(iv)); excerpt (Participation Requirements §2(a)-(b) tag requirement)
sources.used_for: Special Links must carry the Associates tag as a URL parameter (§2(a)-(b), excerpt). Cloaking and redirect-based hiding of the URL are prohibited (v). Link shorteners that make it unclear that the link goes to Amazon are restricted (w). No artificial clicks (s). Amazon Marks may not be used in email or offline material (Trademark Guidelines 3(iv)).
sources.status: verified (2 clauses by excerpt; re-check §2 wording)

sources.used_for: Associates IDs end in '-20' for the US program (the software adds '-20'); additional tracking IDs are requested through Customer Service.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google (rel="sponsored")
sources.used_for: rel="sponsored" marks advertisements and paid placements (commonly paid links). nofollow is an accepted alternative. Google's guidance is that these attributes are hints.

sources.title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers
sources.used_for: Disclosures must be hard to miss, placed with the endorsement, and in the same language. Disclosures that appear only on an About page or behind a 'more' link are likely to be missed. 'sp', 'spon', 'collab' and stand-alone 'thanks' or 'ambassador' are too vague.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 - Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
sources.publisher: U.S. Federal Trade Commission / eCFR (U.S. Government Publishing Office)
sources.used_for: Definition of endorsement (§255.0(b)), general considerations (§255.1), and disclosure of material connections (§255.5). Used as the legal reference for disclosure placement on every page.

sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.used_for: Beef, pork, veal and lamb steaks, chops and roasts: 145 °F, rest at least 3 minutes. All poultry and ground poultry: 165 °F. Ground meats: 160 °F (row added to the thermometer guide on 2026-11-20; re-check against the full chart).

sources.title: Food Thermometers
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.updated: July 9, 2026 (as indicated in the search index)
sources.used_for: Whole poultry: check the thigh, wing and thickest part of the breast, avoiding bone. Poultry parts: insert into the thickest area, avoiding bone.

sources.title: Amazon Associates Central - Application review process (help)
sources.used_for: Associates require at least three qualifying sales within the first 180 days; personal orders do not count. Sites must have robust original content; the help text gives 'at least 10 posts' as a rule of thumb. Tags must be embedded in links on the sites declared in the application.

sources.title: Amazon.com Associates Central - Help: How do I build a simple text link to a specific item on Amazon?
sources.used_for: Amazon-owned description of ASINs ('ASIN is the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products') and the official Associates text-link format (amazon.com/dp/ASIN/...?tag=YOURASSOCIATEID). Update (2026-11-20, session arena63534e5d): an Amazon-owned page was located on the allowlisted Associates Central host; read as a search excerpt, so a manual full-page re-check is still pending (FLG-012).
